newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says 1996 growth will be 1.3 percent.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says 1996 growth will be 1.3 percent.

text.p: French finance minister Jean Arthuis said on Sunday the French economy would grow by 1.3 percent in 1996, meeting the official government forecast.
Speaking in a radio interview on Europe 1, Arthuis said, "We will finish 1996 with growth of 1.3 percent."
The official government forecast for 1996 growth is 1.3 percent.
He said the pace of growth at the end of 1996 would be encouraging and supported the case for an acceleration in economic activity in 1997.
Asked if he planned to raise the government's current 2.3 percent forecast for growth in 1997, Arthuis said, "I confirm that growth in 1997 should be at least 2.3 percent."

"We have, today, a return of growth in France and in other European countries...I think the conditions are there for growth to reach the levels which will allows us to create a sufficient amount of jobs to reduce unemployment."
